findings.rule: Retention must keep exactly the snapshot day and the preceding 29 days, so the prune cutoff must never be derived from a snapshot date in the future relative to the current UTC day.
findings.trigger: Reported against the previous revision (fingerprint c9f1ab86), where SyncDaily pruned with PruneMarketRateSnapshots(day.AddDate(0, 0, -(retentionDays-1))) using the caller-supplied date directly. A future-dated enqueue through the documented seam - client.InsertTx(ctx, tx, jobs.FetchRatesArgs{ScheduledFor: "<future date>"}, nil) - put the cutoff itself in the future, so DELETE FROM market_rate_snapshots WHERE snapshot_date < $1 removed the entire recent published cache in the same transaction and left GET /api/v1/exchange-rates at unavailable/no_snapshot for every pair. No caller in the tree did this, so it was latent rather than an active production failure.
findings.impact: Total loss of the recent market-rate cache and a fully degraded exchange-rate endpoint until the next successful daily sync; applied accounting was never affected because each posted transaction stores its own rate, date and journals.
findings.recommendation: RESOLVED in the revision under review (fingerprint 9b6d7486). internal/rates/service.go:146-153 now computes anchor := day and, when the current UTC instant is before the snapshot day, replaces it with midnight UTC of the current day before subtracting retentionDays-1. I verified by reading that the window is identical to the old behaviour whenever day <= now (TestMarketRateLifecycle/rolling_retention_keeps_thirty_snapshot_days still asserts exactly 30 published rows, oldest 2026-08-18, newest 2026-09-16), and in a throwaway copy I reverted only this clamp and confirmed the new subtest TestMarketRateLifecycle/a_future-dated_job_cannot_prune_the_recent_cache fails while the other nine subtests pass, so the regression test genuinely fails for the original behaviour. No further change is required for this finding. Rejecting or clamping a future snapshot date at the top of SyncDaily would additionally close the residual issue recorded separately below and make this anchor clamp redundant.

findings.rule: A published snapshot must not be dated after the current UTC day, and status=stale must mean the snapshot date is older than the current UTC day, as docs/exchange-rates.md states.
findings.trigger: The anchor fix bounds the prune cutoff but still stores the caller-supplied date verbatim: InsertMarketRateSnapshot writes SnapshotDate: dateValue(day) with no check against s.clock().UTC(). Enqueue a future-dated job through the documented seam (client.InsertTx with FetchRatesArgs{ScheduledFor: "2026-11-15"}) while the current UTC day is 2026-09-20; SyncDaily publishes that 2026-11-15 batch. No production caller does this today (the periodic job always passes time.Now().UTC()), so it is latent, but after the anchor fix it is the only remaining effect of a future-dated job.
findings.impact: The future batch becomes the newest published snapshot, so LatestPublishedMarketSnapshotDate and CurrentMarketRateSnapshot prefer it (ORDER BY snapshot_date DESC) and Rate() serves snapshot_date=2026-11-15 to clients. Because staleness is computed as snapshot_date != today (internal/rates/service.go:219-220) rather than < today, the response is simultaneously status=stale, stale=true and a snapshot_date in the future, which contradicts the documented definition of stale and can present a client with a future-dated batch date for a rate whose rate_date is correctly current. I reproduced that exact payload in a throwaway copy: status=stale, stale=true, snapshot_date=2026-11-15, rate_date=2026-09-16, latest_snapshot_date=2026-11-15, display=1.1 with the injected clock at 2026-09-20. The accounting core remains unaffected.
findings.recommendation: Smallest change: reject or clamp a snapshot date after the current UTC day at the top of SyncDaily (for example return an error when day.After(today), or set day to today) so a future-dated job cannot publish an out-of-window batch; the anchor clamp then becomes redundant. If publishing a future-dated batch is deliberately allowed instead, change the staleness test at internal/rates/service.go:220 to snapshot_date < today and update docs/exchange-rates.md to match. Non-blocking: no present caller can trigger it.

No independent load, soak or multi-replica worker test was run: the concurrency evidence is two simultaneous same-day SyncDaily calls in one process against one database, not two worker processes competing through River leadership, and the daily 17:10 UTC schedule was unit-tested as a pure function rather than observed firing at that wall-clock time.
